key_insight: η-feasible directions enable finite-direction searches for nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization over general convex sets despite boundary geometry that can obstruct standard feasible-direction methods.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports derivative-free constrained optimization when objective evaluations and structural access to a convex feasible set are available.
method: Search feasible segments using exact line searches without accessing the objective’s smooth-minus-convex decomposition.
Use an η-direction oracle to select directions uniformly separated from the feasible-direction cone boundary.
Alternatively, construct spanning directions through noise-augmented randomization using the affine-hull inner normal.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical stationarity and convergence-rate guarantees, including almost-sure d-stationarity of randomized accumulation points, but no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Exact line searches and constraint-geometry access may be costly in practice, and the guarantees rely on stated regularity and direction-set assumptions.
paper_title: Randomized and Oracle-Based Feasible Directions Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Constrained Optimization
